# Agentic Sport Analytics: The Evidence-Contract Field Guide

> *Agentic Sport Analytics* is a comprehensive, evidence-bound guide to building AI-powered sport analytics: capture and calibration, detection and tracking, trajectory recovery, event data, statistics and rating systems, expected value, vision-language models, and the agent harness that turns analysis into coaching action. Every claim is measured in a local laboratory on two real sports — pickleball as the fixed-camera baseline, Australian rugby league as the moving-camera stress test. Written by Mehran Mozaffari (AI Operator & Applied AI Builder based in Sydney, Australia), the book is free for personal use under a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license (code under Apache-2.0/MIT).

## Book Information

*   **Official Website**: [https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/) - Read the full book online.
*   **Book Repository**: [https://github.com/imehr/agentic-sport-analytics](https://github.com/imehr/agentic-sport-analytics) - Download the book's source HTML, PDF, and EPUB files.
*   **Website Repository**: [https://github.com/Piazr/agentic-sport-analysis](https://github.com/Piazr/agentic-sport-analysis) - Repository for the preview website.
*   **Author**: [Mehran Mozaffari](https://github.com/imehr) - AI Operator & Applied AI Builder, Sydney, Australia.

## Part I: Foundations (Watching the Field)

*   [Chapter 1: Why This Book Exists: The Five Verbs of Sport Analytics](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/01.html): Watching, tagging, modelling, interpreting, acting — and why the field's arguments are really about which verb a tool performs
*   [Chapter 2: The Evidence Contract & Data Provenance](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/02.html): The four-tier hierarchy, the claims register, and why "measured" is a word with a disk path
*   [Chapter 3: Sport Rules as Formal Systems](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/03.html): Pickleball and Rugby League grammar: state machines, event semantics, and what vision can never infer
*   [Chapter 5: Data Engineering for Sport Video](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/05.html): Ingest, provenance, the one-spine schema, DuckDB querying, and the golden-fixture regression harness

## Part II: Watching (Capture, Geometry, Perception)

*   [Chapter 4: Capture: Cameras, Lenses, Shutter, Placement](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/04.html): The physics of getting footage your models can use: sensor geometry, motion blur, rolling shutter, and the placement math
*   [Chapter 6: Calibration I: Homography, Intrinsics, Distortion](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/06.html): Why pixels lie, how the camera model works, and the Z-limit that forces multi-view
*   [Chapter 7: Calibration II: Broadcast Dynamics, GMC, and Per-Frame H_t](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/07.html): Why camera-motion compensation is not enough, and what a real broadcast calibration loop looks like
*   [Chapter 8: Detection: YOLO, RF-DETR, and the AGPL Decision](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/08.html): The 2026 detector landscape, the license that shapes your architecture, and the noise floor
*   [Chapter 9: Tracking & Identity: Metrics, ReID, and Role Priors](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/09.html): Why 26 IDs on 4 players matters, which metric tells you the truth, and how role priors repair identity
*   [Chapter 10: Segmentation & Foundation Models: SAM 2/3, DINOv3](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/10.html): Promptable masks, concept segmentation, and the measured cost of pixels over boxes
*   [Chapter 11: The Body in Motion: 2D Keypoints to 3D Biomechanics](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/11.html): What stance tells you, what 2D cannot prove, and the escalation ladder to 3D
*   [Chapter 12: Smashing the Ball Wall: Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Recovery](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/12.html): Why single-frame detectors fail on projectiles, and the physics prior that rectifies them
*   [Chapter 13: Identity: Who Is Who](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/13.html): Track IDs are not people: jersey OCR, ReID embeddings, team clustering, roster priors, and the consent line
*   [Chapter 14: Multi-Camera Geometry, Line Calls, 3D Reconstruction](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/14.html): Why line calls are 3D measurements, how triangulation works, and the cost ladder that makes it real
*   [Chapter 15: Audio & Multimodal Cues: The Free Sensor](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/15.html): Paddle pops, whistles, and crowd roar: why the audio track is your cheapest event detector
*   [Chapter 16: Video Understanding: Action Recognition, Spatio-Temporal](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/16.html): The 2026 recipe, the SoccerNet suite, and the measured gap between describing and deciding

## Part III: Tagging and Modelling

*   [Chapter 17: Event Data &amp; the Common Representation](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/17.html): PBN formalization, rugby's missing schema, and the one-spine standards that make it all queryable
*   [Chapter 18: Annotation: The Ground-Truth Workflow](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/18.html): Tooling, label budgets, inter-annotator agreement, and the discipline that makes labels trustworthy
*   [Chapter 19: Automatic Eventing: State Machines, Confidence, Review Queues](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/19.html): From coordinate streams to coach-ready events without hallucinating a single one
*   [Chapter 20: Statistics for Sport Practitioners](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/20.html): The n-trap, honest confidence intervals, multiple comparisons, shrinkage, Bayesian updates, and the calibration discipline no model chapter can skip
*   [Chapter 21: Rating Systems: DUPR, ELO, Glicko, and Skill](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/21.html): The rating math, the three rival systems, and the honest truth about small samples
*   [Chapter 22: Expected Value: xG, VAEP, EPV, and Their Sport Transplants](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/22.html): The possession-value ladder, pickleball's missing model, and the rugby anchor that needs no tracking data
*   [Chapter 23: Tactical ML: Graphs, Equivariance, and Honest Forecasting](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/23.html): TacticAI's architecture, the rotation test, and why 84.6% on one clip is a hypothesis
*   [Chapter 24: Simulation & Counterfactuals: The Honest Rebuild](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/24.html): What-IF is only well-posed with an explicit response model — and the v1 book proved the cost of forgetting

## Part IV: Interpreting and Acting

*   [Chapter 25: Where Vision-Language Models Help, and Where They Lie](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/25.html): The lie exhibit rebuilt: current models, the grounded critic, and the honesty anchors that say describe, don't decide
*   [Chapter 26: From Numbers to Narrative: Reports, Scouting, Coach UX](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/26.html): The analyst-to-coach bridge, the SportsCode XML contract, and the honesty rules in prose
*   [Chapter 27: The Agent Harness for Sport Analytics](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/27.html): The role registry, the Teamwork loop, and how the book becomes a spec your agents can execute
*   [Chapter 28: The Live Coaching Cockpit: Real-Time Systems, Honestly Measured](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/28.html): The latency budget re-verified, the live/async split, and the alert semantics coaches can trust
*   [Chapter 29: Practice Design & Interventions: The Acting Loop](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/29.html): From match faults to constrained practice, grounded in the coaching science that actually has evidence
*   [Chapter 30: Sensors & Hardware: Wearables, Smart Courts, the Fusion Spine](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/30.html): The verified inventory, the dead-sensor market reality, and the ~$1,500 M4-native rig

## Part V: The Laboratory and the Frontier

*   [Chapter 31: Deployment, Licensing, Rights & Ethics](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/31.html): The AGPL trap, media rights, athlete data, and the no-medical-advice boundary
*   [Chapter 32: The Laboratory: Reproducing the Book's Claims](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/32.html): One runner, every lab, and the status table that separates measured from pending
*   [Chapter 33: The Frontier: What's Changing in 2025-2026](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/33.html): The living chapter — models, hardware, benchmarks, agents, and the staleness triggers that keep it honest
*   [Chapter 34: The Book as a System: How to Use It (Human + Agent)](https://piazr.github.io/agentic-sport-analysis/chapters/34.html): The reader path, the agent path, the chapter dependency graph, the dual-sport navigation map, the reproduction contract, and the update channel
